headings.title: SMTO-GML-0059 — That Gmail label can't be created, renamed or deleted

html:
SMTO-GML-0059 — That Gmail label can't be created, renamed or deleted

GUID: 5accecec-8ec1-5006-a28e-943e8c9de5ec
Slug: gmail-system-label-protected
Domain: GML · Subsystem: gmail_imap

What happened

  • SMTO can only create, rename or delete your own Gmail labels. The label you asked about is one of Gmail's built-in folders, such as Inbox or Sent, or the new name isn't allowed. Nothing was changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Choose one of your own labels, or a new name. Avoid Inbox, the names of Gmail's built-in folders, names starting with [Gmail], blank names, and names over 225 characters. Gmail reserves these names for its own folders, and SMTO refuses them to protect your mailbox.
  2. When asking SMTO to rename a label, include the new name in your request. SMTO can't rename a label without being told what to call it.
  3. To move mail in or out of a built-in folder, ask SMTO to archive, move to Trash, mark read or unread, or star the messages instead. These actions change where messages appear without renaming or removing Gmail's own folders.
  4. Before asking again, look at the label list in Gmail to check whether an earlier request already created or renamed the label. Checking first avoids creating a duplicate or renaming a label twice.

What success looks like

  • The label appears in Gmail's label list with the name you wanted, or disappears after you asked to delete it.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't switch to a different Gmail account to get around this.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The label create/rename/delete was refused because the target is a Gmail system folder, or the new name is empty, longer than 225 characters, contains control characters, equals INBOX or a system folder, or starts with [Gmail], [Googlemail] or a backslash.

What this means

  • The requested label name is invalid or identifies a protected system folder. Confirmed substeps and effect_unknown remain authoritative. This diagnostic alone does not establish whether a prior write or send completed.

Why this can happen

  • Producer condition: The requested label name is invalid or identifies a protected system folder.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the exact account revision, Gateway route and failing substep with the retained receipt.

How to fix it

  • Pass a valid custom label: non-blank, at most 225 characters, no control characters, not INBOX, not a special-use folder name and not prefixed with [Gmail], [Googlemail] or a backslash; update_label also requires a name. For message state use the dedicated archive, read/star or trash actions instead of renaming or deleting system folders.
  • Choose a valid custom label. Use the dedicated archive, read/star or trash actions for message state instead of renaming or deleting Gmail system folders.

Retry and execution caution

  • Preserve confirmed work and establish the current mailbox state before any repeated write.

How to verify the fix

  • The chosen operation completes with a matching receipt, or the remaining uncertain action is inspected in Gmail without duplicate mail.

What not to do

  • Do not switch accounts or authentication methods after failure, or automatically replay uncertain writes.

Technical notes

  • Confirmed substeps and effect_unknown remain authoritative. This diagnostic alone does not establish whether a prior write or send completed.
